entities.name: Electron
entities.how_described: 本集提到团队正在构建一个 Electron 原生应用，Codex 需要通过 Chrome DevTools 协议连接到它

evidence.quote: We wanted Codex to be able to connect to our Electron app.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Still, Codex was connecting to the Electron app over Chrome DevTools protocol, but it was actually a local TypeScript daemon that was being spun up that was providing a little CLI interface instead of the MCP because we found that there were only two or three tool calls that we actually needed, just more context efficient as faster.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: One neat way that we made that idea real in this app we are building is in dev, uh electron app, we had a uh window screen that the agent could launch, uh, which would basically give it the native rendering canvas that we're shipping, as well as our full design system and component library, which means it's actually able to prototype new screens directly in the surface that we're deploying, produce screenshots of them, give them to our designer, and now it's a super, super tight loop on does our vision match the reality?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Uh, to give you an example, in order to get Codex to drive our electron app, before computer use was a thing, we needed to boot up a graphical Ubuntu in a Docker container with a virtual display driver and X server, have engineers install X quartz on their Mac in order to proxy over to that headless host uh and like wire up FFmpeg to this gross contraption in order to record videos of what the app was doing, how the agent had changed it.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Looking at the local development process, we wanted Codex to be able to connect to our Electron app.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Uh still, Codex was connecting to the Electron app over uh Chrome DevTools protocol, but it was actually a local TypeScript daemon that was being spun up that was providing a little CLI interface instead of the MCP because we found that there were only two or three tool calls that we actually needed.
